rows.annotation: PAAR-containing Rhs-family type VI secretion system effector protein.
rows.evidence: The 89.7%-identical P. putida homolog is identified as T6SS effector Tke2, although its reported experiment measures Rsm protein binding rather than catalytic activity. Query domains include PAAR, RHS repeats, an Rhs-associated core and a C-terminal LHH domain; STRING associations with VgrG proteins corroborate T6SS involvement. No substrate-specific fitness data or direct nuclease characterization is supplied. The prePAAR motif label alone does not establish DNA deaminase activity.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier A is supported by convergence of the close homolog's T6SS effector identification, query PAAR/RHS domain architecture and independent STRING associations with VgrG proteins. Available evidence includes computational and experimental homolog summaries, domain annotations, neighborhoods, STRING and topology predictions; the Fitness Browser hit supplies only a YD-repeat annotation, without fitness measurements or cofitness. Specific WHH nuclease and DNA deaminase assignments are rejected because neither catalytic activity nor substrate specificity is experimentally established, and the query's terminal domain is labeled LHH. The comparative adhesin assignment has weaker support than the convergent T6SS evidence.

rows.conservation_breadth:
[[BEGIN CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
Counted over EVERY homolog found for this query, before the per-source display caps that apply to the other evidence blocks.
Distinct organisms with a homolog: 29 (in 10 genera)
Query organism: Pseudomonas putida
Organisms OTHER than the query's own with a homolog: 28 (9 genera other than Pseudomonas)
%Identity to query across these homologs: 30.6-92.0
Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
